chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Inform me about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And for the divorced women a provision with the goodness; this is a right upon the pious.' What is the lowest of that provision when he is financially tight, he cannot find it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'A scarf or something resembling it.'

key_terms.بِالْمَعْرُوفِ: With goodness or in a fair manner
key_terms.مَتَاعٌ: Provision or gift given to a divorced wife

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum financial provision (muta') for a divorced woman if the husband is poor?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the practical application of Quranic verse 2:241, defining the minimum 'matāʿ' (gracious provision) for a financially constrained (muʿsir) husband as a simple headscarf or similar modest item. This interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on flexibility and ease in marital obligations, ensuring that financial hardship does not negate the husband's duty to provide a token of goodwill and dignity to his divorced wife.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Abdul Kareem, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘Inform me about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [2:241] And for the divorced women a provision with the goodness; this is a right upon the pious. What is the lowest of that provision when he was financially tight, he cannot find it?’ Heasws said: ‘A scarf or something resembling it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from Sama‘ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan and Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah all abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following: “About the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘. . . divorced women must be benefited with fairness; it is a right on the pious ones’, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘It is after the end of waiting period, and about, ‘an affluent man and one not-so-affluent each according to their abilities’, he (the Imam) said, ‘Why should he not benefit her during her waiting period when she hopes and he hopes that Allah by His will may make something good to happen for them? An affluent man must benefits his woman with servant and one not affluent, benefit with wheat, (dates), raisins, clothes and dirham. Al-Hassan ibn Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, benefited the woman he divorced with a slave-girl. He (the Imam) benefited all the women he divorced.’” Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sanaa ‘ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a similar Hadith except that he has said, ‘Al-Hassan ibn Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would benefit his women with slave-girls.’”
